verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_clean_html_unchanged: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The module docstring and constant names are clear, but the tokenizer logic is full of single-letter names (s, i, j, k, n, c, q, e, vs, rs, re_) in parse_tag and sanitize, and the complex scanning branches have few inline comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The policy lives in named constants (URL_ATTRS, REMOVE_WITH_CONTENT, CSS_BAD_RE) and there are separate helpers. However, parse_tag and sanitize are long hand-written state machines with nested loops and branches, and regexes are recompiled inline (re.compile(r"--!?>") inside the loop).

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It writes with an explicit encoding via surrogateescape, handles unterminated tags and comments by running to the end of the input, and skips the write when nothing changed. There are many magic regex and character-range constants, and argv validation is not clearly shown.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: Uses general rules throughout: attribute names are lowercased and on* is matched by prefix, URLs are entity-decoded and stripped of control characters before scheme checks, :href, srcdoc, meta refresh, svg animate values and CSS are covered, and tokenizing is browser-like. Chromium reported 0 of 60 payloads firing.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: Edits are byte-preserving and only the offending pieces are removed. But it over-strips: every iframe (with its content), object, embed and base is removed even with a benign URL, and a whole <style> block is emptied on @import. The hidden test test_clean_html_unchanged failed.
